summary: Saphalya Amatya works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Amatya served as Chief Exploration Officer at the Department of Archaeology (attested 1974) and as Editor of Ancient Nepal (attested 1987).
Sara Frumento is an Indology and history and archaeology scholar who studied for a DPhil in Area Studies (South Asia) at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).

Sara L. McClintock is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She studied at Columbia, Lausanne, CIHTS, and Harvard (PhD 2002), working with Tom Tillemans, among others, and held faculty posts at UW–Madison (attested 2003) and Emory (attested 2026).
Sarah Aoife Richardson is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD in 2016 at the University of Toronto under the supervision of Jenny Purtle.

Sarah E. Fraser specializes in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Michigan and Kobe University, she held appointments as an Associate Professor at Northwestern University (1996) and Directrice d'Études at EPHE (2000).

Sarah H. Jacoby specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Yale University (~1993–1997) and the University of Virginia (~2000–2007), and later held posts at Columbia University (2006–2009) and Northwestern University (2009).

Sarah Harding (born 1951) is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied with Kalu Rinpoche and Lama Tenpa. She served as a fellow at the Tsadra Foundation (~2000) and held posts at Naropa University (~1992–2018; 2008).

Sarah J. Horton specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied under Stanley Weinstein at Yale University and served as an Assistant Professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).
Sarah Merkle-Schneider is an Indology scholar who earned an M.A. from the University of Tübingen, where she also held an M.A. post (attested 2026).

Sarah Shaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins. She has held affiliations with Oxford's Faculty of Oriental Studies, Wolfson College, and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).
Saraju Rath is an Indologist and linguist who held positions at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (1906–1983) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who studied under Sivaprasad Bhattacharyya and Jitendra Nath Banerjea. He worked as Librarian at The Asiatic Society (1943) and served as a colleague at the University of Calcutta.

Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) worked in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Presidency University and University of Calcutta. He served as Director of Bhutia Boarding School (1874) and as Tibetan translator for the Government of Bengal (1881–1904).
Sarat Sarma is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Manipur University under the supervision of S. Shyamkishore Singh (attested 2006).

Sarath Piyananda Weerasekara is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Deshapriya Gunasena / G. A. Gamini (attested 2026).

Saroja Bhate (born 1942) is an Indologist and linguist. She served as Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1978–2002) and as Honorary Secretary at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).
Sarva Daman Singh is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who served as Professor of History at the University of Queensland, attested in 1958 and 1987.

Sarvepalli Gopal (1923–2002) was a historian who studied at the University of Madras, Presidency College, Chennai, and Balliol College, Oxford. He held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University from ~1971 to 1983.

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975), a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religion, studied at Madras Christian College and University of Madras. He held professorships at Mysore, Calcutta, and Oxford, and served as Vice-Chancellor of Andhra and Banaras Hindu Universities and Chancellor of Delhi.

Saswati Mutsuddy is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Dipak Kumar Barua. She served as an assistant professor in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011).
